title: Judgment on Judah and Jerusalem

questions.question: For behold, the Lord GOD of hosts is taking away from Jerusalem and from Judah support and supply, all support of bread, and all support of what?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:1 (ESV): "all support of bread, and all support of water;"

questions.question: And I will make boys their princes, and who shall rule over them?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:4 (ESV): "and infants shall rule over them."

questions.question: My people—infants are their oppressors, and who rule over them?
Tell the righteous that it shall be well with them, for they shall eat the fruit of their what?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:10 (ESV): "for they shall eat the fruit of their deeds."

questions.question: Woe to the wicked! It shall be ill with him, for what his hands have dealt out shall be done to whom?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:11 (ESV): "for what his hands have dealt out shall be done to him."

questions.question: For Jerusalem has stumbled, and Judah has fallen, because their speech and their deeds are against the what?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:8 (ESV): "because their speech and their deeds are against the LORD,"

questions.question: The look on their faces bears witness against them; they proclaim their sin like whom?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:9 (ESV): "they proclaim their sin like Sodom;"

questions.question: The LORD has taken his place to contend; he stands to judge his what?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:13 (ESV): "he stands to judge his people." (ESV actually says "judge peoples" in v13, but v14 says "The LORD will enter into judgment with the elders... of his people". Let's check v13 exact wording: "The LORD has taken his place to contend; he stands to judge peoples." Wait, KJV says "people". ESV "peoples". Let's stick to ESV. "peoples".) Correction: "peoples".

questions.question: What do you mean by crushing my people, by grinding the face of the what?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:15 (ESV): "by grinding the face of the poor?"

questions.question: Because the daughters of Zion are haughty and walk with outstretched necks, glancing wantonly with their what?
Therefore the Lord will strike with a scab the heads of the daughters of Zion, and the LORD will lay bare their what?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:17 (ESV): "and the LORD will lay bare their secret parts."

questions.question: In that day the Lord will take away the finery of the anklets, the headbands, and the what?
Instead of perfume there will be rottenness; and instead of a belt, a what?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:24 (ESV): "and instead of a belt, a rope;"

questions.question: Instead of well-set hair, baldness; and instead of a rich robe, a skirting of what?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:24 (ESV): "and instead of a rich robe, a skirting of sackcloth;"

questions.question: And her gates shall lament and mourn; empty, she shall sit on the what?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:26 (ESV): "empty, she shall sit on the ground."

key_verse_text: Tell the righteous that it shall be well with them... Woe to the wicked! It shall be ill with him...
